findings.finding: Set B=(0,0),C=(Fₙ₊₂,0),D=(Fₙ,0),I=(Fₙ,r). Compute F,E via tangency formulas. A=intersection of BF,CE. K=second intersect of circumcircles (ABC) & (AFE). K′=reflect K across EF. N=proj_D onto EF. Circle through B,K tangent to BN ⇒ center O on ⟂BN at B, O·K=|K|²/(2·(O·K)). T=(2Oₓ,0). Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE). For each n, cyclic condition KNK′B ⇒ solve f(r)=0. Two families of roots: small‑r (huge R) and moderate‑r giving R=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. For even n large, small‑r roots disappear, so a_{2n}=max R→F_{2n+2}/F_{2n-1}→φ³=2+√5. Thus α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋=2^{25}=33 554 432. 33 554 432 mod 99 991 = 57447.

Set B(0,0), C(a,0) with a=Fₙ₊₂, D(d,0) where d=Fₙ, e=Fₙ₊₁. I(d,r). Compute F,E via tangency: F=(d(d²−r²)/(d²+r²),2d²r/(d²+r²)), E=(a−e(e²−r²)/(e²+r²),2e²r/(e²+r²)). A=intersection BF & CE. K=second intersect of (ABC) & (AFE). K′=reflect K across EF. N=proj_D_on_EF. Circle through B,K tangent to BN ⇒ center O=t·v⊥, t=|K|²/(2v·K), T=2Oₓ. Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE). Cyclic condition KNK′B ⇒ solve f(r)=0. For each n, roots r give R; moderate root yields R=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁→φ³=2+√5. Small‑r roots give huge R but disappear for large even n, so sup a_{2n}<α=2+√5. Hence p=2,q=5, compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991 =2^{25} mod 99991 =57447.

Set B=(0,0), C=(a,0) with a=Fₙ₊₂, D=(Fₙ,0). Incircle I=(Fₙ,r). Compute F,E via tangency formulas. A=intersection of BF,CE. K=2nd intersect of (ABC) & (AFE). K′=reflect K across EF. N=proj_D onto EF. Circle through B,K tangent to BN ⇒ center O on ⟂BN at B, O·K condition ⇒ O=t·v, t=|K|²/(2v·K). T=2Oₓ on BC. Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE). For the “moderate” solution (r≈mid), R=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁ → φ³=2+√5. Small‑r solutions give huge R but disappear for large n; thus α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991 = 2^{25} mod 99991 = 57447.

Use BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, s free>BC. Compute geometry numerically: A from sides, incircle I=(Fₙ,r), E,F via ratios, K=second intersect of (A,E,F) & circumcircle, K′=reflex across EF, N=proj_D_on_EF. Find s where B,N,K,K′ cyclic (solve f(s)=0). Exclude near‑a degenerate root (s≈a). Proper roots give ratio R=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE). For even n≥4, max R→≈4.99287287… →α=5=5+√0. Then ⌊5^{0⁵}⌋=1 mod 99991. Pitfalls: include degenerate root (huge R) and ensure T may lie off segment (allowed).

Key: For n‑tastic triangles BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂. The cyclic condition forces a unique “moderate” solution with ratio R=BC/Fₙ₋₁=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. As n→∞, R→φ³=2+√5. α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5 ⇒ ⟂2^{5²}=2^{25}=33 554 432 mod 99 991=57 447. Pitfall: ignore spurious small‑r solutions; only bounded branch matters.

Model triangle with BC=Fₙ₊₂, D at (Fₙ,0), incircle I=(Fₙ,r). Vary r∈(0,√(FₙFₙ₊₁)). Compute AB,AC as tangents from B,C to I. Find A, E,F (feet). K = second intersection of circumcircles ABC & AEF. K′=reflect K across EF. N=proj of D onto EF. Circle through B,K tangent to BN at B ⇒ center O on perp to BN at B and perp bisector of BK; T=(2Oₓ,0). Ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE). Impose cyclic K,N,K′,B ⇒ det[[x²+y²,x,y,1]]_{B,N,K,K′}=0. Solve for r (root). Compute R at that r; aₙ=R. For large even n, a_{2n}→α=p+√q (≈?); then compute ⌊p^{q^p}⌋ mod 99991. Pitfalls: correct K selection, sign of tangents, ensure O_Bₓ>0 (T on BC). Use high‑precision mpmath.

Use BC=1, d=Fₙ/Fₙ₊₂→(3‑√5)/2, e=1‑d.  Compute incircle radius r (unknown).  Points:  
F=(d(d²‑r²)/(d²+r²),2rd²/(d²+r²)),  
E=(d+2er²/(e²+r²),2e²r/(e²+r²)).  
A=intersection of BF and CE (t>1).  
K = second intersection of circumcircles (ABC) and (AFE).  
K′ = reflection of K across EF.  
N = projection of D(d,0) onto EF.  
Cyclic condition: N lies on circumcircle of B,K,K′ ⇒ f(r)=|N‑O|‑R=0 (O,R from BKK′).  
Solve f(r)=0 for r>0 (multiple roots).  Max ratio = max_{roots} (CT·NB)/(BT·NE) where T from circle through B,K tangent to BN.  
For large n, d→(3‑√5)/2, the smallest r‑root gives max ratio →α≈p+√q.  
Key: scale BC=1, use analytic geometry, solve f(r)=0 numerically, then compute ratio.  Pitfall: many spurious roots; keep only t>1.  α≈? (to be derived).
α = φ³ = 2+√5 (limit of F_{n+2}/F_{n-1}); p=2,q=5 → ⌊2^{5²}⌋=2^{25}=33 554 432; mod 99991 = 57447. (Key: moderate root gives ratio → a/F_{n-1} → φ³; exclude degenerate small‑r solutions.)

Set B(0,0), C(a,0) with a=Fₙ₊₂, D(d,0) where d=Fₙ, e=Fₙ₊₁. I=(d,r). Compute F,E via tangency formulas, A=intersection BF,CE. K=2nd intersect of (ABC) & (AFE). K′=reflect K across EF, N=proj of D onto EF. Enforce K,N,K′,B cyclic → solve for r. The “proper” root gives ratio R=CT·NB/(BT·NE)=a/Fₙ₋₁→φ³=2+√5. α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5 ⇒ ⌊2^{5²}⌋ mod 99991=57447. Pitfall: discard near‑degenerate r→0 solutions (s≈a) that blow up R.
